commits.summary: VF-010: the own checker's branch probes are budgeted in solver conflicts, not seconds, so the path order is the same on every machine (verification pending)
commits.body:
Engine::probe (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs) gave the other side of a branch as long as all the solver calls so far took, at least a second, of wall-clock time. Pricing#total's regression proof has a feasible side whose probe takes about 1.04 s here, so some runs decided it and found the violation in seconds, and others left it undecided and ran out of time (VF-010). A probe is now given as many conflicts as all the calls so far had, at least PROBE_CONFLICTS (10,000). The Sat trait gains a work limit (set_work_limit, work; lib/src/bmc/sat.rs), and so does the Blaster. For CaDiCaL, the conflicts are counted as the clauses it learns, and a call is stopped through the terminate callback, which CaDiCaL polls on a count of its own steps, so a stop is the same on every run. Bitwuzla has no such limit and keeps the wall-clock budget. The run's deadline stays the user's --timeout. The doc comment's design is kept: an undecided side is decided after the decided paths, with all the time left. Transcripts record a probe's conflict limit, and replay gives it again. The module doc and lib/README.md's sentence on the probe budget say so.

Verified inline: lib/tests/reproducers/vf-010.sh found the violation in 8 of 8 runs at the fix, with identical numbers (6 paths, 12 solver calls, 358,609 clauses). The new test a_conflict_limit_stops_a_call_at_the_same_work_every_time passes, and the logged-solver test now checks that probes, and only probes, carry the conflict limit and that a replay gives it again. Every lib test suite passed: 204 unit tests, and integration.rs's 64, JBMC's small cases included.

Jobs: 20261107-165544-vf-010-s-reproducer-at-the-fix-pricing-t and 20261107-165544-vf-010-s-integration-tests-at-the-fix-li close VF-010 when both pass. 20261107-165544-vf-010-s-benchmark-at-the-fix-run-1-of-2 (at this commit) and 20261107-165544-vf-010-s-benchmark-at-the-fix-s-parent-r (at the parent, c307e721) record the own checker's benchmark runs, and a later quick job compares the two.

commits.summary: VF-011: the own checker counts a loop's unwinding per entry of the loop, so an inner loop gets --unwind iterations per outer iteration (verification pending)
commits.body:
Engine::jump (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs) counted each back edge over the whole path, so a nested quantifier's inner loop ran out of --unwind across the outer loop's iterations, and example 052's property was left to JBMC under strict ('a loop was not fully unwound with --unwind 16'). Counts are now kept per frame, by loop head, and a back edge from 'from' to 'target' starts again the count of every head after 'target' up to 'from' (the loops in its body), as JBMC's --unwind counts. It stays a bound: on a path that never ends, the lowest head it keeps returning to is restarted only by back edges to lower heads, taken finitely often, so its count passes the bound and the path ends unwound with no verdict; calls stay at most 64 deep. Merges keep the lower count per frame.

Reproducer, committed with the fix: new unit tests an_inner_loop_is_unwound_per_entry_of_it (4 x 3 nested iterations under --unwind 4, and 052's shape, a sum over i < k inside a loop over k < n), a_loop_is_unwound_per_call_of_its_method, both failing before the fix with 'not fully unwound' and passing after, and a_loop_entered_again_by_an_outer_back_edge_is_bounded_by_the_outer_count (an outer loop beyond the bound, and two overlapping loops, still unwound). Every lib suite passed inline: unit 207, integration.rs 64, conformance, heap, observations, alignment and the rest.

Job 20261107-171502-vf-011-example-052-under-strict-on-the-o runs 052 under strict on the own checker (approach.engine set to native in a copy of examples/) and closes VF-011 when every obligation is established with no gap.
